To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a single GC-rich silencer in the H1t promoter is sufficient to repress its transcription, and that its effect is dominant over that of all other elements.
H1t promoter activity depends on the integrity of the cap-proxi-mal silencer and that the AC and TG boxes are required for full silencer activity.
a GC-rich silencer in the H1t promoter dominates the expression pattern in most cells and that the TG/AC element, a conserved motif found in all H1 genes, is required for promoter function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel testis-specific histone gene and the mechanisms that regulate its expression.
the role of the cap-proproximal silencer in the H1t gene.
the transcriptional regulation of the H1 gene family, which includes the testis-specific histone 1t gene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the H1t promoter is a typical histone 1 promoter with a dominant silencer.
the H1t gene is not a “normal” histone 1 promoter, but rather is a “normal” H1 promoter with a dominant silencer element that is active in all cells.
the H1t promoter is a composite of two distinct elements, a silencer and an activator unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cap-proximally located silencer is the major negative regulatory element of the H1 promoter, but it is not the only one.
the H1t gene is controlled by a single silencer, which acts to repress the otherwise constitutive expression of the gene.
the silencer element is a dominant repressor, but it can be overruled by the presence of other activating elements.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the H1t silencer is a powerful repressor of H1t gene expression, which is likely to act in concert with a positive regulatory mechanism to ensure its restricted pattern of transcription.
the H1t promoter is not only a good model of a testis-specific promoter but also a good example of a tissue-specific gene with a dominant negative element.
the H1t promoter is highly sensitive to the cap-proximally positioned silencer, and this is the first demonstration that the silencer and AC elements are functionally interdependent.
